summary: Whitefish Mountain lookout, Flathead NF: 1938 pole tower destroyed 1974; its 1978 steel successor, moved from Ingalls, was removed in 1993 to private land and still stands.

facts.design: 1938: 50' pole L-4 tower; 1978 replacement: 35' steel 7x7' tower moved from the Ingalls lookout
facts.status_note: The 1938 tower was destroyed in 1974; the 1978 steel tower was moved in 1993 to private land near Whitefish and stands there

access.note: The relocated tower stands on private property near Whitefish, per the Forest Fire Lookout Association list and the 2022 Whitefish Pilot article. No public access is described.

corrections.why: The original 1938 tower was destroyed in 1974, but its 1978 steel successor was moved in 1993 to private land; the 2022 Pilot article and the FFLA list both describe it as standing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Pilot describes a tower that stood near Big Mountain. Firelookout.com and SummitPost say the 1978 tower near Big Mountain came from the Ingalls lookout. Taken together, the tower in the yard appears to be the 1978 structure, not the 1938 original.

sources.title: History lives on through former Stoltze vice president

notes_for_editor: Height is disputed: 35 feet (firelookout.com, SummitPost) against 40 feet (Pilot). The story reports the disagreement and does not choose. The Pilot names the owner; the story leaves him unnamed. SummitPost is a climbing site. The story uses it for the 35-foot height of the Ingalls Mountain lookout tower, which SummitPost says moved to the Stolz site in 1978; firelookout.com gives the same height and move for the steel tower.The staffing as_of 1965 is the last couple listed, not a confirmed final year. The original 1938 site has no current description in any source read. Access is private: the FFLA list marks the relocated tower's location private, and the story does not say whether visitors are allowed.
